lines.speaker: Robin
lines.text: I have twelve notes from the briefing, but the volunteers only have ninety seconds before the desk opens. Here’s the short version: the catalog is moving to a new system next month.

lines.speaker: Keira
lines.text: That is too definite. The library is preparing a test migration next month. A full move has not been approved.

lines.speaker: Robin
lines.text: Good catch. The main point is that a batch of three hundred public records will be copied into a test system during the week beginning May twelfth.

lines.speaker: Keira
lines.text: Yes. The old catalog will remain available in read-only mode, so visitors can still search it while the test is checked.

lines.speaker: Robin
lines.text: The part that matters for front-desk volunteers is what visitors will see. They may be invited to try a separate test search, but normal access will continue through the old catalog.

lines.speaker: Keira
lines.text: Also say that no original images or descriptions are being deleted. Copying records for a test is not the same as replacing the source archive.

lines.speaker: Robin
lines.text: In practical terms, volunteers should use the old catalog for service requests and give the test link only to visitors who choose to provide search feedback.

lines.speaker: Keira
lines.text: Correct. Feedback is optional and should concern search results, not personal account details.

lines.speaker: Robin
lines.text: Do they need the names of all seven mapped fields and the three checksum stages?

lines.speaker: Keira
lines.text: No. Those details explain how the team will test accuracy, but volunteers only need to know that the sample will be checked before any wider decision.

lines.speaker: Robin
lines.text: I’ve left out the vendor history, the export file names and the rejected color schemes. None changes what volunteers do next month.

lines.speaker: Keira
lines.text: That is sensible. Keep the number of records, the test week, the read-only source, the optional feedback and the fact that full migration is undecided.

lines.speaker: Robin
lines.text: What about the twelve hundred restricted records?

lines.speaker: Keira
lines.text: Mention that they are outside this test. Do not say they failed or were excluded permanently; their access rules need a separate review.

lines.speaker: Robin
lines.text: Then the short version shouldn’t change “not included in this batch” to “will never be moved.”

lines.speaker: Keira
lines.text: Exactly. It also should not say the new search is faster. The test will measure search accuracy and response time; we do not have results yet.

lines.speaker: Robin
lines.text: Let me try the full ninety seconds: three hundred public records, one test week, old search still available, optional feedback, restricted records outside scope and no full-migration decision.

lines.speaker: Keira
lines.text: Add who to contact if a visitor sees a wrong date or missing creator name: send the item number to the archive desk rather than editing anything at the front desk.

lines.speaker: Robin
lines.text: So one action line, one open issue and no technical tour. That is much clearer than reading my twelve notes in order.

lines.speaker: Keira
lines.text: Yes. A useful summary follows the listener’s task, but every sentence must still be traceable to the longer briefing.
